SELECT STATEMENT.what: returns the rows of the query
SELECT STATEMENT.normal: The top of every query plan.

INSERT STATEMENT.normal: The top of an INSERT plan.

UPDATE STATEMENT.normal: The top of an UPDATE plan.

DELETE STATEMENT.normal: The top of a DELETE plan.

MERGE STATEMENT.normal: The top of a MERGE plan.

TABLE ACCESS FULL.normal: Small tables, or when a large share of the rows is needed: multiblock reads beat thousands of single-block index reads.
TABLE ACCESS FULL.suspicious: A big table of which only a few rows are needed.
TABLE ACCESS FULL.check: Is there an index on the filter columns? Is the predicate written so that an index can be used (no function or conversion on the column)?

TABLE ACCESS STORAGE FULL.what: reads the whole table (Exadata smart scan)
TABLE ACCESS STORAGE FULL.normal: Exadata offloads the filter to the storage cells.
TABLE ACCESS STORAGE FULL.suspicious: Same as TABLE ACCESS FULL for a few rows of a big table.

TABLE ACCESS BY INDEX ROWID.what: reads table rows by the rowids the index returned
TABLE ACCESS BY INDEX ROWID.normal: Few rowids, or rows stored in index order (good clustering factor).
TABLE ACCESS BY INDEX ROWID.suspicious: Many rowids with a filter discarding most of them after the read.
TABLE ACCESS BY INDEX ROWID.check: Can the filter columns be added to the index?

TABLE ACCESS BY INDEX ROWID BATCHED.what: reads table rows by rowids, grouped by block
TABLE ACCESS BY INDEX ROWID BATCHED.normal: The 12c+ form of index access: fewer block visits.
TABLE ACCESS BY INDEX ROWID BATCHED.suspicious: Many rowids with a filter discarding most of them.
TABLE ACCESS BY INDEX ROWID BATCHED.check: Can the filter columns be added to the index?

TABLE ACCESS BY USER ROWID.what: reads a row by a rowid given in the query

TABLE ACCESS BY LOCAL INDEX ROWID.what: reads partition rows by rowids from a local index
TABLE ACCESS BY LOCAL INDEX ROWID.suspicious: Many rowids discarded by a filter.

TABLE ACCESS BY GLOBAL INDEX ROWID.what: reads partition rows by rowids from a global index
TABLE ACCESS BY GLOBAL INDEX ROWID.suspicious: Many rowids discarded by a filter.

TABLE ACCESS BY INDEX ROWID BATCHED (LOC.what: reads partition rows by rowids from a local index

TABLE ACCESS SAMPLE.what: reads a sample of the table

TABLE ACCESS CLUSTER.what: reads rows of a table cluster

TABLE ACCESS HASH.what: reads rows of a hash cluster by the hash key

INDEX UNIQUE SCAN.what: finds at most one row in a unique index
INDEX UNIQUE SCAN.normal: Lookup by a primary or unique key: the cheapest access.

INDEX RANGE SCAN.what: reads a range of index entries
INDEX RANGE SCAN.normal: Equality on a non-unique key or a range on the leading columns.
INDEX RANGE SCAN.suspicious: A range that returns a large part of the table, or no access predicate (the whole index is filtered).
INDEX RANGE SCAN.check: Leading columns of the index are in the access predicate.

INDEX RANGE SCAN DESCENDING.what: reads a range of index entries in descending order
INDEX RANGE SCAN DESCENDING.normal: ORDER BY ... DESC served by the index.

INDEX FULL SCAN.what: reads the whole index in key order
INDEX FULL SCAN.normal: Avoids a sort for ORDER BY, or MIN/MAX.
INDEX FULL SCAN.suspicious: No STOPKEY above and many rows: the whole index is read block by block.
INDEX FULL SCAN.check: Is the order needed? Pagination (FETCH FIRST / ROWNUM) above makes it cheap.

INDEX FULL SCAN (MIN/MAX).what: reads only the first or the last index entry
INDEX FULL SCAN (MIN/MAX).normal: MIN/MAX of an indexed column: very cheap.

INDEX FULL SCAN DESCENDING.what: reads the whole index in descending key order
INDEX FULL SCAN DESCENDING.normal: ORDER BY ... DESC served by the index.
INDEX FULL SCAN DESCENDING.suspicious: No STOPKEY above and many rows.

INDEX FAST FULL SCAN.what: reads the whole index like a table (multiblock, unordered)
INDEX FAST FULL SCAN.normal: The index has all the needed columns and is smaller than the table (COUNT(*), covering index).

INDEX SKIP SCAN.what: probes the index once per distinct value of its leading column
INDEX SKIP SCAN.normal: The leading column has few distinct values.
INDEX SKIP SCAN.suspicious: Many distinct values in the leading column: many probes.
INDEX SKIP SCAN.check: Is there an index that starts with the columns of the predicate?

INDEX SAMPLE FAST FULL SCAN.what: reads a sample of the index

BITMAP INDEX SINGLE VALUE.what: reads the bitmap of one key value
BITMAP INDEX SINGLE VALUE.normal: Bitmap indexes on low-cardinality columns (data warehouses).

BITMAP INDEX RANGE SCAN.what: reads bitmaps of a range of key values

BITMAP INDEX FULL SCAN.what: reads all bitmaps of the index

BITMAP CONVERSION TO ROWIDS.normal: Bitmap access, or B-tree indexes combined through bitmaps.
BITMAP CONVERSION TO ROWIDS.suspicious: Over B-tree indexes: a composite index may be better.

BITMAP CONVERSION FROM ROWIDS.what: turns rowids into bitmaps to combine indexes
BITMAP CONVERSION FROM ROWIDS.suspicious: Over B-tree indexes: a composite index may be better.

NESTED LOOPS.what: for each row of the first child runs the second child
NESTED LOOPS.normal: Few outer rows and a cheap (indexed) inner access.
NESTED LOOPS.suspicious: Many outer rows, or a full scan on the inner side: the inner side is repeated that many times.
NESTED LOOPS.check: Rows of the first child and the access method of the second.

NESTED LOOPS OUTER.what: nested loops keeping outer rows without a match

NESTED LOOPS ANTI.what: nested loops keeping outer rows that have no match (NOT EXISTS / NOT IN)

NESTED LOOPS SEMI.what: nested loops keeping outer rows that have a match (EXISTS / IN)

HASH JOIN.what: builds a hash table from the first child and probes it with the rows of the second
HASH JOIN.normal: Joining many rows with equality conditions.
HASH JOIN.suspicious: A huge build side (may spill to TEMP) or only a few rows needed (nested loops could be cheaper).
HASH JOIN.check: The smaller input should be the first child.

HASH JOIN OUTER.what: hash join keeping rows of the probe side without a match

HASH JOIN RIGHT OUTER.what: hash join keeping rows of the build side without a match

HASH JOIN ANTI.what: hash join keeping rows without a match (NOT EXISTS / NOT IN)

HASH JOIN ANTI NA.what: null-aware anti join (NOT IN over nullable columns)
HASH JOIN ANTI NA.normal: The efficient form of NOT IN.

HASH JOIN RIGHT ANTI.what: anti join with the subquery as the probe side

HASH JOIN SEMI.what: hash join keeping rows with a match (EXISTS / IN)

HASH JOIN RIGHT SEMI.what: semi join with the subquery as the build side

HASH JOIN BUFFERED.what: parallel hash join that buffers the probe rows

MERGE JOIN.normal: Inputs already sorted, or non-equality joins.

MERGE JOIN CARTESIAN.what: joins every row of one input with every row of the other
MERGE JOIN CARTESIAN.normal: One side has a single row (a constant, an aggregate) or star queries.
MERGE JOIN CARTESIAN.suspicious: Both sides have many rows: usually a join condition is missing.
MERGE JOIN CARTESIAN.check: Join conditions between the tables of the two sides.

SORT JOIN.what: sorts an input of a merge join

BUFFER SORT.what: keeps the rows in memory to reuse them
BUFFER SORT.normal: Under a Cartesian join or a loop: the rows are read once and reused.

SORT ORDER BY.what: sorts the rows for ORDER BY
SORT ORDER BY.suspicious: Huge inputs may spill to TEMP.

SORT ORDER BY STOPKEY.what: keeps only the top N rows while sorting

SORT GROUP BY.suspicious: Huge inputs may spill to TEMP.

SORT GROUP BY NOSORT.what: groups rows that already come sorted

SORT AGGREGATE.what: computes an aggregate over all rows (one result row)
SORT AGGREGATE.normal: COUNT/SUM/MAX without GROUP BY: no real sort.

HASH GROUP BY.what: groups the rows with a hash table
HASH GROUP BY.suspicious: Huge inputs may spill to TEMP.

HASH UNIQUE.what: removes duplicates with a hash table

WINDOW SORT.what: sorts the rows for analytic functions
WINDOW SORT.suspicious: Huge inputs may spill to TEMP.

WINDOW SORT PUSHED RANK.what: sorts for ROW_NUMBER/RANK keeping only the top rows

WINDOW BUFFER.what: computes analytic functions over sorted rows

WINDOW NOSORT.what: computes analytic functions over rows that come sorted

COUNT STOPKEY.what: stops after N rows (ROWNUM <= N, FETCH FIRST)
COUNT STOPKEY.normal: Pagination: the steps below stop early.

FILTER.what: discards rows by a condition; with two or more children it runs the subqueries for the rows of the first one
FILTER.normal: A simple condition, or a subquery for few rows.
FILTER.suspicious: A subquery that runs for many rows: it was not unnested into a join.
FILTER.check: Rows of the first child; can the subquery be written as a join or EXISTS?

VIEW.what: returns the rows of a view or an inline query
VIEW.normal: A view that was not merged into the main query.

VIEW PUSHED PREDICATE.what: a view evaluated for each outer row with the join condition pushed into it

UNION-ALL.what: appends the rows of all children

UNION ALL PUSHED PREDICATE.what: union all with the join condition pushed into each branch

CONCATENATION.what: appends the branches of an OR condition (OR expansion)
CONCATENATION.normal: Each OR branch uses its own index.

INLIST ITERATOR.what: repeats the step below for each value of an IN list
INLIST ITERATOR.normal: IN list on an indexed column.

MINUS.what: rows of the first child that are not in the second

PARTITION RANGE ITERATOR.normal: Pruning to the partitions of the predicate.

PARTITION RANGE ALL.suspicious: The predicate has the partition key but pruning did not happen (function or conversion on the key).
PARTITION RANGE ALL.check: The partition key in WHERE without functions.

PARTITION RANGE INLIST.what: reads the partitions of an IN list

PARTITION RANGE AND.what: reads partitions matching several pruning conditions

PARTITION LIST ALL.suspicious: The partition key is in the predicate but pruning did not happen.

TEMP TABLE TRANSFORMATION.what: materializes WITH subqueries into temporary tables first
TEMP TABLE TRANSFORMATION.normal: A WITH subquery used several times.
TEMP TABLE TRANSFORMATION.suspicious: Used once: materialization is extra work.

LOAD AS SELECT.what: writes rows directly into a segment (direct path or a temp table)

COLLECTION ITERATOR PICKLER FETCH.what: reads the rows of a collection or a pipelined function (TABLE(...))
COLLECTION ITERATOR PICKLER FETCH.suspicious: The optimizer does not know how many rows a collection has: the default guess is 8168.
COLLECTION ITERATOR PICKLER FETCH.check: CARDINALITY hint or a real row count.

COLLECTION ITERATOR CONSTRUCTOR FETCH.what: reads the rows of a collection constructor

CONNECT BY WITHOUT FILTERING.what: hierarchical query over all rows at once

CONNECT BY NO FILTERING WITH START-WITH.what: hierarchical query from the START WITH rows

REMOTE.what: sends a query over a database link
REMOTE.suspicious: Inside a loop, or without a WHERE clause (the whole remote table comes over the network).
REMOTE.check: The remote SQL (Remote SQL section of the Text tab).

PX COORDINATOR.what: collects the results of parallel processes

PX SEND QC (RANDOM).what: parallel processes send rows to the coordinator

PX SEND HASH.what: parallel processes redistribute rows by hash

PX SEND BROADCAST.what: parallel processes send every row to all consumers

PX BLOCK ITERATOR.what: splits a table into block ranges for parallel processes

STATISTICS COLLECTOR.what: counts rows at run time to choose between adaptive plan branches

RESULT CACHE.what: returns results from the result cache when possible

MAT_VIEW REWRITE ACCESS FULL.what: reads a materialized view instead of the tables (query rewrite)

FAST DUAL.what: returns one row without reading DUAL

UPDATE.what: updates the rows coming from below

DELETE.what: deletes the rows coming from below

MULTI-TABLE INSERT.what: inserts into several tables (INSERT ALL / FIRST)

columns.Step: The reading order: children before their parent, the first child first. It shows who starts producing rows first, not exact timing - many operations are pipelined.
columns.Id: The operation number in PLAN_TABLE and in the DBMS_XPLAN text (Text tab).
columns.Operation: What the step does. Hover for the description.
columns.Name: The table, index or view the step works on.
columns.Rows: Estimated rows per one execution of the step. A step on the inner side of nested loops runs once per outer row: its total is about Rows x the outer Rows.
columns.Cost: Optimizer cost of the step with everything below it, in internal units (not milliseconds). Not additive for nested loops, so the cost of a step alone cannot be computed by subtraction.
columns.Time: A rough time estimate derived from the cost.
columns.Pstart/Pstop: First and last partition read. KEY: decided at run time from binds; KEY(AP)/KEY(SQ): pruning by a subquery; ALL: every partition.
columns.access: How rows are located: the condition used to find them (an index range, a join key).
columns.filter: What is discarded after the rows were read: the work is done anyway.

PRED-01.title: Conversion on column {column}
PRED-01.detail: {call} is applied to every row, so an index on {column} cannot be used to find them. Usually the compared value has another type: compare with a value of the column's own type{type}.
PRED-01.normal: A function-based index on exactly this expression makes it indexable.

PRED-02.title: Implicit conversion of DATE column {column}
PRED-02.detail: {call}: the DATE column is converted for every row - typically compared with a TIMESTAMP (Java/JDBC binds). An index on {column} cannot be used.
PRED-02.normal: INTERNAL_FUNCTION also appears for IN lists and LOB/XML; here the column is a DATE.

PRED-02C.title: INTERNAL_FUNCTION on column {column}
PRED-02C.detail: {call}: Oracle transforms the column before comparing. Often an implicit conversion (DATE vs TIMESTAMP), then an index on the column cannot be used.
PRED-02C.normal: INTERNAL_FUNCTION also appears for IN lists, LOB/XML and collations.

PRED-03.title: Join of columns of different types
PRED-03.detail: {call} in a join condition: the column is converted for each row, so its index cannot drive the join (nested loops become full scans).

PRED-04.title: Function on indexed column {column}
PRED-04.detail: {call}: a regular index on {column} cannot be used for this condition.
PRED-04.normal: A function-based index or a virtual column on this expression; or rewrite the condition without the function (e.g. a date range instead of TRUNC).

PRED-05.title: Linguistic comparison on {column}
PRED-05.detail: {call}: NLS_COMP=LINGUISTIC (session setting) makes the comparison linguistic, and a regular index on {column} cannot be used.
PRED-05.normal: A linguistic index (NLSSORT function-based index) matching NLS_SORT.

ACC-01.title: Full scan of a big table for a few rows
ACC-01.detail: {table} has {numRows} rows in {blocks} blocks; the optimizer expects {rows} rows ({share}) after the filter.{indexed}
ACC-01.normal: If the filter is not selective in reality, or the index has a bad clustering factor, the full scan can be right.

ACC-01I.title: Full scan is reasonable
ACC-01I.detail: {table}: about {share} of the rows are needed - reading the whole table with multiblock reads is usually cheaper than index access.

ACC-02.title: Index read without an access condition
ACC-02.detail: {index} is scanned with a filter only: the whole index (or a large part) is read and then filtered.
ACC-02.normal: INDEX FULL/FAST FULL SCAN to avoid a sort or for COUNT is fine.

ACC-04.title: Most rows found by the index are discarded
ACC-04.detail: {index} returns ~{indexRows} rowids, the table filter keeps ~{rows}: each discarded row cost a table block read. Columns of the filter: {columns}.
ACC-04.normal: Adding the filter columns to the index lets it discard rows before the table is read.

ACC-08.title: Index {index} is {state}
ACC-08.detail: {index} on {columns} could serve this condition, but it is {state}.
ACC-08.normal: An invisible index may be intentional (being tested).

JOIN-01.title: Cartesian join
JOIN-01.detail: Every one of ~{left} rows is joined with every one of ~{right} rows: usually a join condition is missing.
JOIN-01.normal: Fine when one side has a single row or the result is small (star queries).

JOIN-01I.title: Cartesian join of small inputs
JOIN-01I.detail: ~{left} x ~{right} rows: cheap here, probably intentional.

JOIN-02.title: Full scan inside nested loops
JOIN-02.detail: {table} is read in full for each of ~{outer} rows of step {outerStep}.
JOIN-02.normal: Fine for a tiny table that stays in the buffer cache.

JOIN-04.title: Database link call inside nested loops
JOIN-04.detail: The remote query runs for each of ~{outer} rows of step {outerStep}: a network round trip per row.
JOIN-04.normal: Fine when the outer side has one or two rows.

PART-01.title: No partition pruning on {table}
PART-01.detail: All partitions are read although the predicates use the partition key ({key}). A function or conversion on the key usually prevents pruning.

PART-01I.title: All partitions of {table}
PART-01I.detail: The predicates do not use the partition key ({key}), so every partition is read.

SUBQ-01.title: Subquery runs for each row
SUBQ-01.detail: FILTER at step {step}: the subquery (step {subStep}) runs for each of ~{outer} rows of step {outerStep}; it was not unnested into a join.
SUBQ-01.normal: Cheap when the outer rows are few or the subquery results repeat (they are cached).

SUBQ-01I.title: Subquery for a few rows
SUBQ-01I.detail: FILTER at step {step}: the subquery runs for ~{outer} rows only.

NOTE-01.title: Hint {meaning}: {hint}
NOTE-01.detail: The optimizer reported this hint as {meaning}{reason}. A hint that does nothing is dead code or a typo.

NOTE-02.title: Dynamic sampling
NOTE-02.normal: With fresh statistics sampling still happens for complex predicates, correlated columns or SQL plan directives.

NOTE-02I.title: Dynamic sampling with fresh statistics
NOTE-02I.detail: {note} The statistics are fresh: sampling is due to complex predicates, correlated columns, SQL plan directives or temporary tables.

NOTE-03.title: The plan is fixed
NOTE-03.detail: {note} Changing the query may not change the plan in production.

NOTE-04.title: Adaptive plan
NOTE-04.detail: {note} The join method may switch at run time; inactive rows are hidden on the Plan tab.

CARD-04.title: Default estimate for a collection
CARD-04.detail: {object} is estimated at {rows} rows - the optimizer's default guess for collections, not a real count.
CARD-04.normal: Hint CARDINALITY(alias N) or DYNAMIC_SAMPLING with a realistic size.

banners.binds: The statement has bind variables: EXPLAIN PLAN does not peek at their values (default selectivity) and treats them as VARCHAR2, so the real plan may differ; conversions applied to binds are artifacts of EXPLAIN.
banners.adaptive: Adaptive plan: the final choice is made at run time.
banners.fixed: A SQL plan baseline, profile or patch applies: production will use the fixed plan.
banners.estimate: This is the optimizer's estimate (EXPLAIN PLAN), not a measurement: "expects", not "took".
